It's a Windham Weaponry VEX-SS “Varmint Exterminator”. Boy, that's a mouthful. Guess I'll call it "Vex". I paid out of my ass for this thing with bullshit euro prices, and waited 9 months to get it due to an unforeseen amount of bullshit spanning 3 different governments. Finally it is mine. And now its winter. Fuck gubment.

Anyway, its your basic AR15, but with a special barrel.

It's 20 inches, rifle gas, heavy varmint profile, stainless steel, with an extra tight "competition" chamber, and a bolt factory matched to the star chamber, for a tight fit. Besides that its pimped out with a round, aluminum, free floated hand and a neat looking neoprene covered buttstock.

The end result should be a sub moa semi automatic rifle, that also resists opening up the group size after being subjected to a longer sting of fire. They don't promise those stats, but that is what you hope for with this kind of barrel, otherwise, there is no point to the weight. Some reviews i read claimed easy 1 moa groups even with basic ammo, and 0.5 moa with match grade. Well, my initial impressions are pretty good.

Target: https://i.imgur.com/EadTZqw.png

I shot this in a 100m, wind free zeroing tunnel. I was shooting at 50m due to the shitty 150$, 1-4x optic i put on it. I'm pretty sure the 5th shot was my fuck up, so the math works out to an exact 1moa group at 100m. Even counting in the 5th shot, and making it a 2 moa group, i'm impressed with the gun considering the conditions.

  • the optic is low light trash, and with a 2moa center dot, so its kind of tricky to shoot a group smaller than the dot itself
  • the ammo was not match grade, but basic bitch S&B 55gr FMJ
  • the barrel only had the most rudimentary 20 shot break in
  • the barrel probably did not have a popper copper deposit from the previous 10ish shots from zeroing
  • the trigger is a basic shitty gritty mil-spec at 5lbs
  • i had a front sand bag, but no sand sock in the back, just a bunched up fist
  • the bench was some kind of standing bench at the wrong height
  • the rifle had me behind the trigger :D

Considering all that, even a 2 moa group would have satisfied me, but as i said, I'm pretty sure i saw myself pull the 5th shot. So out of the box, the accuracy is amazing. This is not a gucci AR. I will report back in half a year when i test out all the match grade stuff.

 

To name some negatives:

The trigger is mil-spec. It's kind of shit. Was gritty out of the box and must be at least 5 lbs pull. After releasing it 100 times onto my palm, and shooting 100 rounds, it cleaned up a bit, but it's still a 5 lbs pull. Good for grunts, but unworthy of a DMR style rifle. But i understand their logic. If they put in a 250-400$ match trigger, it would boost the price of the rifle at least 30%. And while people might be willing to pay that for a match trigger, they probably demand a very specific one. Single stage, two stage, Geissele, Triggertech, etc., not one picked by Windham. So it kind of makes sense to just put in a 20$ mil-spec trigger and keep the rifle cheaper. Have the user pay for exact one he wants later on.

But now i have entered the living hell of "what fucking trigger do i chose?!?!?" At first, i will do a DIY trigger job, but ultimately I'm probably gonna have to shake my self upside down for a Geissele trigger. If you know anything that is "just as good" but costs half as much, let me know. I also need a non-crap optic, probably a 2-10x PST 2, but that's another topic. For now i have another 4-16x44 el cheapo Primary Arms that is way better than the 1-4x24.

The openings in the hand-guard have not been made MLOK compatible. It's not the kind of rifle you attach things anything to besides a sling + bi-pod, and for that you have provisions. But they could have made the extra effort to make it MLOK sized slots, and machine small flat spots inside. As it is, if someone wanted to mall ninja it, he would have to improvise a bit.

There is some wobble between the lower and the upper. From what I'm seeing, it's the standard amount, and it can be addressed, but i would be happier if it just wasn't there. Just an AR thing i guess. Speaking of AR things, the recoil sucks. Because it does not exist. At the same time, the recoil is awesome. Because it does not exist.

The barrel is not threaded. They sell the barrel + matched bolt as a kit, and they offer it in both threaded an un-threaded. But they chose the un-threaded version for the complete rifle. I don't actually need the thread, but i wonder why would anyone build a rifle without a thread in 2019.

It's heavy. 8.2 lbs unloaded with no optic. The barrel is incredibly thick. It's fluted on the outside, but even with that, it's heavier then the Vietnam era "government rifle". Slap on a scope + cantilever mount, and I'm at 10lbs unloaded. I'm sure you could build an AR10 that is under 10lbs. Maybe that's the price one has to pay to have that kind of performance when it comes to precision + consistency under heat + velocity.

 

My logic was, if men marched through entire wars with the weight of an M1, M14, and FAL, then I'll be damned if I'm gonna bitch over my AR being 10 lbs. After the test tunnel, i went to another range that has some fancy training programs for swat and special forces, where you have a film being projected on a 10 meter wide wall, and some kind of sensor system to detect your shots. It's not suppose to be for civilians, but as soon as the RO saw my green CARGO PANTS and a DEATH BLACK semi rifle in hand, he was all "psst, kid, you wanna kill some human pixels?"

It consist of various room and backyard clearing footage, where a bunch of guys are jumping out at you, shouting threats and insults. After a minute of talking shit, they ether go away or suddenly pulling a gun and shoot at you. You are suppose to only shoot the armed perps and if you do, the system instantly dubs a kill animation over that spot on the screen. It's pretty obvious from that description that i basically had to hold the rifle up with sights on people for 15 minutes straight. After 10 minutes, of a fully extended grip, i just had to switch to a mag-well grip.

 

So that's the reality of it. It's a MK12 DMR, not an MK18 CQB. With that being said, 2 years ago i had a 200 lbs one rep max bench, before i broke my leg and abandoned the gym. I have a feeling that back then i would have wondered why anyone would buy a light rifle.
